what: Rocket Companies is the largest mortgage lender in the United States. It originates and services home loans, and after buying Mr. Cooper and Redfin it now also runs a large servicing book and a property search portal.
customers: American homebuyers and people refinancing, plus investors who buy the loans it originates.
money: gain on sale of home loans
growing after the Mr. Cooper purchase
fees for collecting payments on mortgages
Redfin property search, title and closing services
moat: A brand that American borrowers recognise and a technology platform that closes loans faster than branch-based lenders, now paired with a servicing book that feeds it refinancing customers.
risks: Mortgage volumes collapse when rates rise and surge when they fall, so earnings are very cyclical
Integrating Mr. Cooper and Redfin at the same time is a large undertaking
It pays no dividend and the founder controls voting power
opportunities: The servicing book provides fee income that rises when origination falls, balancing the cycle
A fall in mortgage rates would set off a refinancing wave it is built to capture
watch: Origination volume and market share, and servicing portfolio size.
